title: Comparison of mitragynine and 7‐hydroxymitragynine concentrations, antioxidant properties, and volatile profiles of kratom (Mitragyna speciosa (Korth.) Havil.) infusions through household brewing methods
content:
Abstract

Background

Kratom (Mitragyna speciosa (Korth.) Havil.) is increasingly prepared as a botanical beverage, but direct comparisons of household brewing methods remain limited. This study compared boiling, moka pot percolation, and cold brewing to determine how preparation method affects mitragynine and 7-hydroxymitragynine concentrations, antioxidant properties, and volatile profiles.

Results

Mitragynine and 7-hydroxymitragynine were quantified by ultrahigh-performance liquid chromatography coupled with high-resolution tandem mass spectrometry (UHPLC–high-resolution MS/MS), antioxidant properties were assessed by DPPH (2,2-diphenyl-1-picrylhydrazyl), FRAP (ferric-reducing antioxidant power), and total phenolic content assays, and volatile compounds were profiled by headspace-solid-phase microextraction-gas chromatography–mass spectrometry (HS-SPME-GC–MS). Boiling produced the highest mitragynine concentration and the strongest antioxidant responses, while 7-hydroxymitragynine remained low. Moka pot brewing gave intermediate alkaloid and antioxidant values and a volatile profile with greater contributions from aldehydes, benzenoids, ketones, and furans. Cold brew contained the lowest mitragynine concentration and showed weaker DPPH and FRAP responses, with a milder volatile profile and the highest measured 7-hydroxymitragynine concentration among the three brewing methods.

Conclusion

The household brewing method changed the measured alkaloid, antioxidant, and volatile composition of kratom infusions. Boiling favored mitragynine and antioxidant extraction, whereas moka pot and cold brewing produced distinct chemical profiles. These results provide compositional data for comparing consumer-relevant preparation methods without inferring clinical safety or pharmacological effects from beverage chemistry alone. © 2026 Society of Chemical Industry.
